channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Spring break travelers at Houston’s Hobby Airport face hours-long wait times amid government shutdown
item.description: The estimated wait time was three hours as of Monday morning, according to the Houston Airport System, which cited a shortage of TSA workers.

item.title: In a clown’s shoes: How bull fighters and barrelmen protect cowboys at the Houston rodeo
item.description: They put themselves between the bulls and their riders, who are often unable to defend themselves after rides. The idea is to distract the animals while the cowboys run out of the ring.

item.title: KP George’s money laundering trial to start after appeals court denies bid to remove Fort Bend DA from case
item.description: Last week, George lost the GOP primary for Fort Bend County judge, securing 8.4% of the vote to place last in a five-candidate race.

item.title: Hello Houston (March 9, 2026)
item.description: Today: We discuss the rise in oil prices due to the Iran conflict, learn about the upcoming Brains in Society conference, talk with Houston chef Jassi Bindra about competing in the new season of “Top Chef,” and more.

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (March 9, 2026)
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters, we have – The Commuter Cut – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: Energy prices soar to levels not seen in years as Iran names new supreme leader and digs in
item.description: The price for a barrel of Brent crude, the international standard, surged to $119.50 per barrel early in the day Monday. The average price of gas in Houston has jumped to more than $3 per gallon.

item.title: Texas businesses could wait years for tariff reimbursements — if they come at all — despite court rulings
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that more than $126 billion in emergency tariffs were illegally collected, and the U.S. Court of International Trade said the Trump administration must refund them.

item.title: Man fatally shot by Houston police after barricading himself inside house, authorities say
item.description: A SWAT team officer shot and killed a 36-year-old Black man who allegedly walked out of a home with a "high-powered rifle" and fired at least one shot, according to police.

item.title: Texas Democrats Goodwin, Vélez hope to keep voters engaged ahead of lieutenant governor runoff
item.description: Texas Democrats busted through turnout expectations for the primaries. But can they keep up that momentum for May's runoff elections? State Rep. Vikki Goodwin and labor organizer Marcos Vélez — the Democratic candidates facing off to challenge incumbent Republican Lt. Gov Dan Patrick — certainly hope so.

item.title: UTMB’s multimillion-dollar partnership with ‘Blue Zones’ to bring health-conscious changes to Galveston
item.description: The Blue Zones Project partners with municipalities, healthcare providers, schools and employers to emulate practices from healthy hotspots around the world.
